findings.source_passage: her three tall tapering masts mildly waved to that languid breeze, as three mild palms on a plain
findings.why_it_matters: This simile—three masts as three mild palms on a plain—is distinctively rhythmic and imagistic, establishing the dreamy serenity before the squid's appearance; its loss flattens the tonal setup.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'her three tall tapering masts mildly waved to that languid breeze, as three mild palms on a plain' in the opening paragraph.

findings.source_passage: furlongs in length and breadth, of a glancing cream-colour, lay floating on the water
findings.why_it_matters: The source specifies 'furlongs in length and breadth,' an emphatic measure of the creature's enormous scale; the draft drops 'furlongs in length and breadth,' stripping interpretive force from the description of the squid's size.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'furlongs in length and breadth' before 'of a glancing cream-colour' to preserve the hyperbolic scale that defines the creature's strangeness.

findings.source_passage: though other species of whales find their food above water, and may be seen by man in the act of feeding, the spermaceti whale obtains his whole food in unknown zones below the surface; and only by inference is it that any one can tell of what, precisely, that food consists
findings.why_it_matters: This passage carries critical-interpretive weight: it establishes the sperm whale's fundamentally hidden, inferential nature—a thematic keystone for the novel's epistemology—and is erased entirely from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the contrast between surface-feeding whales and the sperm whale's unknown-depth feeding, including the 'only by inference' clause, in the closing expository section.

findings.source_passage: in swarming-time the bees rush to the boughs
findings.why_it_matters: The draft renders this 'as bees to the boughs,' dropping 'in swarming-time,' which gives the simile its seasonal specificity and rhetorical texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'as in swarming-time the bees rush to the boughs' for the full simile.

findings.source_passage: The manner in which the Bishop describes it, as alternately rising and sinking, with some other particulars he narrates, in all this the two correspond
findings.why_it_matters: The draft cuts the specific cross-referencing of the squid's rising-and-sinking behavior to Bishop Pontoppidan's Kraken description, losing the comparative naturalist reasoning that anchors the passage's scholarly voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the sentence noting that the Bishop's description of alternating rising and sinking corresponds to the squid's behavior, to preserve the evidentiary reasoning.

summary: The draft preserves most of the chapter's famous passages but loses three medium-severity items—the 'furlongs in length and breadth' scalar detail, the complete 'three tall tapering masts as three mild palms' simile, and the critical interpretive passage on the sperm whale's wholly unknown subsurface feeding ('only by inference')—triggering regeneration.
